symptom: `refresh catalog full source` took 5.5 min on a 4,753-unit MPR v2 app on macOS and 90+ min for users on Windows, where `full` alone takes 9 s; agent-driven builds on Windows ran hours behind the same input on a Mac. The cost grows with the square of the project
cause: Each source describe (up to 8 in parallel) found its microflow with `microflowsNamed`, which lists every microflow unit, and the duplicate-output-variable warning resolved each called flow with `GetRawUnitByName`, which lists every unit of the type; `GetMicroflow(id)` listed them all too. Nothing held the reads, so one refresh opened 7,532,649 .mxunit files. An open costs microseconds on a warm macOS cache and around a millisecond under Windows Defender's real-time scan
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_catalog.go` (`buildCatalog`: `CacheUnitReads` scope over the whole build), `modelsdk/mpr/reader_units.go` (`Reader.UnitByID`), `modelsdk/mprread/generic.go` (`UnitByID[T]`) behind `mdl/backend/modelsdk/microflow.go` `GetMicroflow`, `mdl/executor/helpers.go` (`pinnedMicroflow`, used by `describeMicroflowMode` when the build pinned `describeID`), `mdl/executor/validate_void_code_calls.go` (`microflowID`: called microflows read by ID)
insight: **Count file opens, not seconds: the platform gap is per open.** The same refresh is minutes on a Mac and hours on Windows, so a wall-time report from one platform says nothing about the other, and a Mac benchmark hides the bug. A temporary build with a global counter next to `r.fileReads.Add(1)` gave the platform-free number; the CPU profile (83% syscall under `listUnitsByTypeV2In`) named the two callers. The narrow lookups cut the reads 9,818 → 4,092 on pedapp, and the profile then showed a tail of other per-describe listings (Java action lookups via `containerSetForModule`, `describeNanoflow`'s `ListMicroflows`, the XPath enricher's `ListDomainModels`); fixing them one by one would not end, so the build-wide `CacheUnitReads` is what bounds opens at one per unit (11,017 → 409 on pedapp). A unit's ID is its document's $ID on both formats (checked on a v1 and a v2 project), which is what makes a by-ID read possible without any listing. Guard: `TestSourceCatalogBuild_ReadsUnitFilesLinearly` (reads ≤ units, failing at 11,017 without the fix) and `TestUnitByID_AgreesWithTheListing` on v1 and v2
